subject: humanities
passage: Although it is called the Bayeux Tapestry, the eleventh-century work that depicts the events leading to the Norman conquest of England in 1066 is not a tapestry at all: its images are not woven into the cloth but embroidered on it in colored wool. Nearly seventy meters long, it was probably stitched in England within a generation of the conquest, most likely in a workshop at Canterbury. Because the hanging was produced by several embroiderers, scholars have studied the ______ techniques closely, noting small differences in the way figures are outlined and filled that may show where one worker's section ends and another's begins.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The techniques belonged to "several embroiderers," so the word in the blank must be plural and possessive. A plural noun ending in s forms its possessive by adding only an apostrophe: "embroiderers'."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A plural noun ending in s takes only an apostrophe to show possession; "embroiderers's" is not standard.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Embroiderers" is a plain plural with no apostrophe, so it does not show that the techniques belonged to them.
explanation.C: Correct. "Embroiderers'" is the plural possessive, showing that the techniques belonged to the several embroiderers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Embroiderer's" is the possessive of one embroiderer, but the text says several embroiderers produced the hanging.
